codebook_title: Existential Analysis & Logotherapy Four Fundamental Motivations (4FMs) Codebook
primary_thematic_domains: Four Fundamental Motivations (4FMs) of Existential Analysis
description: A comprehensive codebook for interpretive thematic analysis based on the four fundamental themes of existence (4FMs), used to interpret participant testimony in psychological interventions. All themes, sub-themes, and details are sourced exclusively from the provided academic literature.

4FMs_Codebook.FM_Name: First Fundamental Motivation: Being in the World (Acceptance of Reality)
4FMs_Codebook.FM_Core_Task: Coming to terms with the reality of one's existence, or 'being in the world'[cite: 1080, 1677].
4FMs_Codebook.Exclusion_Criteria_Psychopathology: Phobic and anxiety disorders (in the extreme of this failure)
4FMs_Codebook.Justification_Quote: The corresponding existential need is the need for support, space, protection, and security. If this confrontation fails, the person cannot accept the conditions of existence and reacts with anxiety. [cite_start]In the extreme of this failure, we find phobic and anxiety disorders. [cite: 1147, 1148]

4FMs_Codebook.FM_Name: Second Fundamental Motivation: Living One's Life (The Will to Live, Value)
4FMs_Codebook.FM_Core_Task: Coming to terms with the reality of one's life[cite: 1080, 1677].
4FMs_Codebook.Coping_Reaction: Depressive moods (if a person is not able to experience the value of life)
4FMs_Codebook.Exclusion_Criteria_Psychopathology: Depression (affective disorder, mood disorder) (in the extreme)
4FMs_Codebook.Justification_Quote: The existential need corresponding to the 2nd Fundamental Motivation is the need for value, feeling and value-relation. If a person is not able to experience the value of life, the relationship to life becomes restricted, leading to depressive moods. [cite_start]In the extreme, this restriction is experienced as a depression (affective disorder, mood disorder). [cite: 1152, 1154]

4FMs_Codebook.FM_Name: Third Fundamental Motivation: Being Oneself (Identity, Authenticity, Justice)
4FMs_Codebook.FM_Core_Task: Coming to terms with an awareness of one's identity[cite: 1080, 1677].
4FMs_Codebook.Coping_Reaction: Hysterical reaction of seeking a role (if unable to stand up for one's own identity)
4FMs_Codebook.Exclusion_Criteria_Psychopathology: Histrionic or borderline personality disorders (in the extreme)
4FMs_Codebook.Justification_Quote: The existential need of the 3rd Fundamental Motivation is the need for justice, respect, appreciation, and self-worth. The corresponding failure leads to a person being unable to stand up for one's own identity; it leads to an hysterical reaction of seeking a role. [cite_start]In the extreme, this can be observed as histrionic or borderline personality disorders. [cite: 1164, 1165]

4FMs_Codebook.FM_Core_Task: To participate and be open to relationships and wider contexts from which personal meanings are discovered[cite: 1081, 1678].
4FMs_Codebook.Coping_Reaction: Frustration of meaning (existential vacuum) (if the need is frustrated)
4FMs_Codebook.Exclusion_Criteria_Psychopathology: Addictions, loss of identity (psychosis), and suicidal intentions (in the extreme of this failure)
4FMs_Codebook.Justification_Quote: The 4th Fundamental Motivation refers to the need for meaning, goal, purpose, and future. If this need is frustrated, a person is not able to experience an appeal or a *challenge* in the situation, the individual experiences frustration of meaning (existential vacuum). [cite_start]In the extreme of this failure, we find addictions, loss of identity (psychosis), and suicidal intentions. [cite: 1172, 1173]
